Observed traffic is not maximum speed. Zero traffic does not prove an internet outage.

Weeks start on Monday; months follow the local calendar. Closed snapshots retain original bounds and timezone. Later Beacon imports do not rewrite a snapshot.
Medians and percentiles use mergeable distributions with relative error below 1%; never averages of medians. P90 requires 10 values and P95 requires 20. Measured zero is valid; missing remains missing.
Coverage uses only data support: up to 1 s for Dishy history, 5 s for Beacon or 2 s for status. Retention may reduce coverage. Power and energy use valid intervals only.
Speed comparison uses only scheduled tests in matching 6-hour windows, with three valid results and two days in each period. Smart, manual and extreme tests are shown separately.

High confidence: coverage and days ≥80%, ≥100 latency readings, gap below 6 h and previous coverage ≥80%. Medium: coverage/days ≥40/50% and ≥20 readings. Otherwise low.\nTrends: speed ≥10% and ≥5 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload; latency ≥10% and ≥3 ms; loss/availability ≥0.5 pp; interruptions ≥2; offline time ≥20% and ≥1 min. Telemetry comparisons require coverage ≥40% and a coverage difference ≤20 pp.\nOverall health uses availability, loss, latency and interruptions, never speed alone. It does not attribute causes.
Local generation roughly every 6 hours, when Android allows. No new collection or network access. Force stop may defer work until reopening the app.
Each point represents a day. Gaps indicate no valid metric. Medians are approximate.
There are no readings for this period yet. Keep monitoring with the app or Beacon to build local history.
